result.topic_en: Concluding the classification of the forms the temperature function u can take in the heat-conduction prize problem (cases m = 3 and m = 4), then remarking on forming the differential equations and on the question of when one quadratic differential form can be transformed into a given one.
result.transcription:
11.

e numero finito terminorum formae
$f(t)\,e^{\lambda t}$,
in quibus $\lambda$ constans et $f(t)$ functio integra ipsius $t$ est, aut formam induere
$\varphi(\beta,t)\chi(\alpha,\beta)+\alpha\varphi_1(\beta,t)+\varphi_2(\beta,t)$;
si [-si-] $m=3$, functionem $u$ aut esse e numero finito terminorum $f(t)e^{\lambda t}$ conflatam aut formae
$\varphi(\beta,t)\alpha+\varphi_1(\beta,t)$.
Denique casus $m=4$ nullo negotio penitus absolvi potest. Si enim praeter aequationem $\Delta u=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ habentur tres aequationes inter $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2}$, $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$, $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}$, $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$, $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}$, aut prodibit aequatio formae $r\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}+s\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}$ $(=0)$ et proin variabiles independentes ita eligere licebit, ut $u$ fiat functio unius tantum variabilis, aut $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha^2}$, $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\alpha\partial\beta}$, $\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial\beta^2}$ ideoque etiam $\Delta u$, $\Delta^2 u$, $\Delta^3 u$ per $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\alpha}$, $\frac{\partial u}{\partial\beta}$ exprimi possunt. Tum autem emerget aequatio formae
$a\frac{\partial^3 u}{\partial t^3}+b\frac{\partial^2 u}{\partial t^2}+c\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}=0$,
$u$ habebit formam
$p e^{\lambda t}+q e^{\mu t}+r$ vel $(p+qt)e^{\lambda t}+r$
patetque per praecedentia, $\lambda$ et $\mu$ esse constantes.
Jam sumta $p$ pro variabili independente $\alpha$ et substitutis his expressionibus in aequatione $\Delta u=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ invenitur fieri non posse, ut $q$ sit functio ipsius $\alpha$, siquidem $\lambda$ et $\mu$ sint inaequales. Ergo $p$ et $q$ vice variabilium independentium $\alpha$ et $\beta$ fungi possunt. Praeterea ex aequatione $\Delta u=\frac{\partial u}{\partial t}$ invenitur $r=$ const.
In hoc igitur casu $u$ aut est functio ipsius $t$ et unius tantum variabilis, aut alteram utram formarum
$\alpha e^{\lambda t}+\beta e^{\mu t}+$ const., $(\alpha+\beta t)e^{\lambda t}+$ const.
induet, valore $\mu=0$ non excluso.

Postquam formae, quas functio $u$ induere potest, inventae sunt, aequationes differentiales $F_\nu=0$, quas brevitati consulentes perscribere noluimus, facillimae sunt formatu. Unde in singulis quibuscunque casibus et forma $\begin{pmatrix} b_{1,1} & b_{2,2} & b_{3,3}\\ b_{2,3} & b_{3,1} & b_{1,2}\end{pmatrix}$ et forma, cui adjuncta est $\begin{pmatrix}\beta_{1,1} & \beta_{2,2} & \end{pmatrix}$ innotescit. Si jam in expressionibus $\sum\beta_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in locos quantitatum $s_1,s_2,s_3$ substituuntur functiones quaelibet ipsarum $x_1,x_2,x_3$, manifesto obtinebuntur casus omnes, in quibus $u$ functio temporis et duarum tantum variabilium fieri possit. Unde quaestio prior soluta est.
Superest, ut quaeramus, quando expressio $\sum\beta_{\iota,\iota'}ds_\iota ds_{\iota'}$ in formam datam $\sum\alpha_{\iota,\iota'}dx_\iota dx_{\iota'}$ transformari possit.

items.english: The differential equations F_ν = 0, which for brevity we did not wish to write out, are very easy to form.
Hence the first question is solved.
